title: The package coefficient rings satisfy the completed adic datum
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with its extended $\ell$-adic absolute value, valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Put $I=(\varpi)$ and $A_n=R/(\varpi^n)$ for $n\ge1$. The absolute value is nonarchimedean; $R$ is a Noetherian domain and discrete valuation ring, with maximal ideal $I$ and finite residue field of characteristic $\ell$. Each $A_n$ is a finite ring killed by $\ell^n$, and the canonical quotient transitions $A_{n+1}\to A_n$ are surjective. The complex $[R\xrightarrow{\varpi^n}R]$ in degrees $-1,0$ is a finite free resolution of $A_n$; in particular $A_n[0]$ is perfect [def-pc-perfect-ring-complex]. Thus $(R,I,(A_n))$ satisfies every ring hypothesis of [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum]. For any scheme $T$ the integral coefficient sheaf supplied by this datum is $R_T=\varprojlim_n(A_n)_T$; the integral constructible domain [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] uses modules over this completed sheaf, derived completeness and reductions in one common finite cohomological interval. Under the reindexing $n=m+1$ this is the same quotient system $R/I^{m+1}$, $m\ge0$, used in the smooth coefficient statements. No identification with the discrete constant integral coefficient sheaf is asserted.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value] to the given finite extension and [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr] to its extended absolute value. They give the nonarchimedean inequality, the subring $R\subset E$, the nonzero maximal ideal $I=(\varpi)$, the principal ideal domain property and finite residue field. A subring of a field is a domain, and every ideal is generated by one element, hence is finitely generated; therefore $R$ is Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring].

The extension property and [def-weil-l-adic-numbers] give $|\ell|_E=\ell^{-1}<1$. Thus $\ell\in I=(\varpi)$, so write $\ell=\varpi c$ with $c\in R$. Raising to the $n$-th power shows $\ell^n=\varpi^nc^n\in(\varpi^n)$; multiplication by $\ell^n$ on $A_n$ is zero. The residue field is nonzero and is killed by the prime $\ell$, so its characteristic is exactly $\ell$. In particular its additive group is torsion.

Apply Padic.finite_coefficientExtensionRing from [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension] for finiteness. The canonical transition is Ideal.Quotient.factor, whose surjectivity is Ideal.Quotient.factor_surjective, the transition clause of [lem-weil-valued-dvr-finite-quotients]. Apply the finite-extension clause of [lem-weil-pbc-standard-quotients-perfect] to the same E, uniformizer and positive n. Retain its specified complex, differential, derived isomorphism and quotient augmentation. Its quasi-isomorphism also supplies perfectness with the standard derived-category instance used by adicQuotientPerfect.

In [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] take A to be the actual coefficient integer ring and I its recorded uniformizer ideal. Noetherianity follows from its principal ideal ring instance; I is finitely generated by Submodule.fg_span_singleton. The first quotient is finite by Padic.finite_coefficientExtensionRing at exponent one, so every element has finite additive order (isOfFinAddOrder_of_finite). The preceding step supplies all positive finite and perfect quotients. These fields construct the required datum with ideal equality by reflexivity. The arithmetic construction is universe-polymorphic and does not rely on the larger-site specialization pbcPadicCoefficientDatum.

For schemes satisfying the hypotheses of [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], that definition selects objects in the derived category of modules over this $R_T$ by derived completeness, uniformly bounded constructible reductions and compatible etale-origin witnesses. This is the integral domain referred to in the statement. Finally $n=m+1$ is an order-preserving bijection from $m\ge0$ to $n\ge1$: its quotients and every transition map are literally $R/I^{m+1}$ and the identity-induced quotient maps. Thus the smooth notation describes the same tower. All these constructions use the limit sheaf specified in [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum].
